EUI values provided on each card specify how much that measure will contribute to building loads in each category. Example within the Lighting category: - Card 16 (“No Changes to Lighting”) specifies that the baseline conditions of the building consist of 10 kBtu/ft2 for the lighting load. And because the T8 lights generate heat, there is a +3 kBtu/ft2 contribution to the cooling load and a -3 kBtu/ft2 credit toward the heating load. - Card 11 (“LED Upgrade”) contributes only 5 kBtu/ft2 to the building’s lighting load. And because LEDs generate less heat compared to T8s, the magnitude of this measure’s impact on heating and cooling loads is reduced (+1.5 kBtu/ft2 to cooling and -2 kBtu/ft2 to heating). Once your team has reviewed the options and considered the goals you set in Step 1, select one card from each color category to assemble your retrofit package for the building. Step 3: Calculate Retrofit EUI and Costs Enter the relevant details from your selected cards into the Energy Savings Table (1.5) to determine the EUI and capital cost of the retrofit package you create. Then, proceed to the bottom of this table to calculate the overall savings and payback period. If you have time, make changes to the retrofit options selected to better align with the team’s goals for the project. Be prepared to discuss the reasons for making any changes. 7 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Step 4: Summarize Findings Return to the Overview Table (1.3), where you initially documented your team’s goals for the project, to summarize your findings. Be prepared to explain how your choices addressed your stated goals, how the selected retrofit package did/didn’t meet these goals, and what else may result from the choices you made.
